name: Theory Playground
quip: Foam, strings, notes—and a very honest question mark
lesson: The Planck length is well defined; what lies below present knowledge is not. This entire opening layer is a playful gallery of unconfirmed ideas—foam, strings, vibration, topology—not a claim that any of them are real objects.

curios.name: foam bubble
curios.fact: Spacetime foam is a speculative image for Planck-scale geometry; no experiment has photographed it.

curios.name: vibrating string
curios.fact: Fundamental strings are a mathematical proposal, not experimentally observed threads.

curios.name: resonance note
curios.fact: The music note is a joke about vibration modes, not evidence that spacetime literally makes sound.

curios.name: vacuum shimmer
curios.fact: A quantum vacuum is not classical emptiness, though this visible shimmer is purely playful language.

curios.name: geometry pulse
curios.fact: This pulse is a visual metaphor for unknown Planck-scale geometry, not an observed object.

curios.name: causal uncertainty
curios.fact: Known physics does not yet provide an experimentally tested description of causality at the Planck scale.

curios.name: topology question
curios.fact: Quantum gravity might alter how geometry is described, but no microscopic topology has been observed.

curios.name: extra-dimensional chord
curios.fact: Extra dimensions appear in some theories, but this glowing chord is delighted speculation.

name: Particle Probe Frontier
quip: The map resumes at the edge of experiment
lesson: There is no confirmed ladder of constituents between the Planck scale and present particle probes. This frontier marks experimental limits without inventing material to fill the gap.

curios.name: field ripple
curios.fact: Modern particle physics describes fields extending through space.

curios.name: energy packet
curios.fact: Particles are excitations of fields—not tiny classical beads.

curios.name: unresolved structure
curios.fact: This object is intentionally labeled unknown rather than inventing a particle.

curios.name: measurement horizon
curios.fact: Below current experimental reach, uncertainty should remain visible.

curios.name: symmetry echo
curios.fact: Symmetries organize modern particle theories, but unknown new physics may lie beyond present experiments.

curios.name: field excitation
curios.fact: In quantum field theory, particles are excitations of underlying fields.

curios.name: unknown resonance
curios.fact: This deliberately unnamed resonance represents possibilities that experiments have not established.

curios.name: probe limit
curios.fact: Smaller structure requires higher-energy probes; present measurements set limits rather than revealing a ladder.

name: Quarks & Gluons
quip: Point-like in probes, confined in matter
lesson: Quarks and gluons are experimentally established, while quarks remain consistent with point-like particles at current resolution. This field is a scale metaphor—not a claim that ordinary space is filled with quark–gluon plasma.

curios.name: up-quark trace
curios.fact: Up quarks help make protons and neutrons, but cannot be collected as isolated free objects.

curios.name: down-quark trace
curios.fact: Down quarks are confined by the strong interaction.

curios.name: gluon field
curios.fact: Gluons carry the strong force and bind quarks.

curios.name: quark–antiquark pair
curios.fact: High-energy interactions can produce pairs that hadronize into composite particles.

curios.name: strange-quark trace
curios.fact: Strange quarks appear in short-lived hadrons but are not isolated as free particles.

curios.name: charm-quark trace
curios.fact: Charm quarks are heavy quarks produced in energetic interactions.

curios.name: color-field knot
curios.fact: Color charge is the charge of the strong interaction; it is unrelated to visible color.

curios.name: gluon spray
curios.fact: Energetic quarks and gluons form jets of hadrons rather than emerging alone.

name: Hadron Forge
quip: Composite matter finally has an inside
lesson: Protons and neutrons are hadrons made from quarks and gluons. Their roughly femtometre-scale structure is experimentally measured.

curios.name: proton
curios.fact: A proton contains two up valence quarks and one down valence quark plus gluons and a dynamic quark sea.

curios.name: neutron
curios.fact: A neutron contains one up and two down valence quarks, plus gluons and a quark sea.

curios.name: pion
curios.fact: Pions are mesons made from a quark and an antiquark.

curios.name: antiproton
curios.fact: Antimatter has opposite quantum numbers and annihilates with corresponding matter.

curios.name: kaon
curios.fact: Kaons are mesons containing a strange quark or antiquark.

curios.name: lambda baryon
curios.fact: A lambda baryon contains up, down, and strange valence quarks.

curios.name: rho meson
curios.fact: Rho mesons are extremely short-lived quark–antiquark states.

curios.name: delta baryon
curios.fact: Delta baryons are excited relatives of protons and neutrons.

name: Nuclear Heart
quip: Whole atoms have not arrived, but their centers have
lesson: Atomic nuclei are compact quantum systems made from protons and neutrons. Nuclear size grows roughly with the cube root of nucleon count, not in direct proportion to atomic diameter.

curios.name: deuteron
curios.fact: A deuteron is the nucleus of heavy hydrogen, containing one proton and one neutron.

curios.name: helium-4 nucleus
curios.fact: A helium-4 nucleus contains two protons and two neutrons and is also called an alpha particle.

curios.name: carbon-12 nucleus
curios.fact: Carbon-12 has six protons and six neutrons in its nucleus.

curios.name: fission fragment
curios.fact: Heavy nuclear fission produces energetic daughter nuclei rather than tiny pieces of classical solid.

name: Atomic Cloud
lesson: Atoms are nuclei surrounded by electron probability clouds. The familiar planetary-orbit picture is useful art, not a literal trajectory.

curios.name: hydrogen atom
curios.fact: Hydrogen is one proton with one electron in its neutral state.

curios.name: helium atom
curios.fact: Most helium nuclei have two protons and two neutrons.

curios.name: carbon atom
curios.fact: Carbon's bonding flexibility underpins known life.

curios.name: oxygen atom
curios.fact: Oxygen readily forms bonds, including those in water.

curios.name: nitrogen atom
curios.fact: Nitrogen has seven protons and is central to proteins and nucleic acids.

curios.name: silicon atom
curios.fact: Silicon is abundant in Earth's crust and foundational to modern electronics.

curios.name: iron atom
curios.fact: Iron nuclei sit near the peak of nuclear binding energy per nucleon.

curios.name: uranium atom
curios.fact: All uranium isotopes are radioactive; uranium has 92 protons.

name: Molecular Assembly
lesson: Molecules are stable arrangements of atoms bound by shared or transferred electrons. Their three-dimensional shapes control much of chemistry.

curios.name: water molecule
curios.fact: A water molecule is bent, not linear, with an angle of about 104.5 degrees.

curios.name: glucose
curios.fact: Glucose stores chemical energy and supplies carbon for cells.

curios.name: amino acid
curios.fact: Amino acids are building blocks of proteins.

curios.name: lipid
curios.fact: Lipids can self-assemble into membranes.

curios.name: methane
curios.fact: Methane has one carbon bonded tetrahedrally to four hydrogens.

curios.name: carbon dioxide
curios.fact: Carbon dioxide is a linear molecule with one carbon and two oxygen atoms.

curios.name: caffeine
curios.fact: Caffeine is a relatively small organic molecule that blocks adenosine receptors.

curios.name: salt formula unit
curios.fact: Solid sodium chloride forms an ionic lattice rather than separate NaCl molecules.

name: Macromolecule Reef
lesson: Proteins, DNA, membranes, and many viruses occupy the nanometre-to-hundreds-of-nanometres range. Viruses are not cells.

sources.label: Viruses at the edge of life

curios.name: protein complex
curios.fact: Proteins fold into three-dimensional structures that perform cellular work.

curios.name: DNA loop
curios.fact: DNA is a polymer whose sequence carries genetic information.

curios.name: membrane vesicle
curios.fact: Phospholipid membranes can self-assemble into closed vesicles.

curios.name: small virus
curios.fact: Viruses depend on host cells to reproduce and are not universally considered alive.

curios.name: ribosome
curios.fact: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into proteins.

curios.name: antibody
curios.fact: Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins whose binding regions recognize molecular targets.

curios.name: collagen fiber
curios.fact: Collagen proteins assemble into strong structural fibers in animals.

curios.name: bacteriophage
curios.fact: Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria.

name: Virus Garden
quip: Tiny packages built to borrow a cell
lesson: Viruses span a broad range of nanometre-scale forms. Their capsids and envelopes have recognizable structures, but viruses depend on host cells for reproduction.

sources.label: Viruses at the edge of life

curios.name: influenza virion
curios.fact: Influenza virions carry segmented RNA inside a protein shell and lipid envelope.

curios.name: adenovirus
curios.fact: Adenoviruses have an icosahedral capsid with fibers projecting from its vertices.

curios.name: coronavirus virion
curios.fact: Coronaviruses are enveloped RNA viruses whose spike proteins form a crown-like fringe.

curios.name: giant virus
curios.fact: Some giant viruses are larger than many bacteria and carry unusually large genomes.

name: Cellular Sea
lesson: Many eukaryotic cells are around 10–100 micrometres across. Cells are deformable, internally structured systems—not simple balls.

curios.name: bacterium
curios.fact: Bacteria are cells without a membrane-bound nucleus.

curios.name: red blood cell
curios.fact: Human red blood cells are flexible biconcave discs about 7–8 micrometres wide.

curios.name: yeast cell
curios.fact: Yeasts are single-celled fungi.

curios.name: plant cell
curios.fact: Plant cells have cellulose walls, chloroplasts in photosynthetic tissue, and large vacuoles.

curios.name: white blood cell
curios.fact: White blood cells are diverse immune cells rather than one single cell type.

curios.name: neuron
curios.fact: Neurons transmit information through electrical and chemical signaling.

curios.name: amoeba
curios.fact: Amoebae change shape using extensions called pseudopodia.

curios.name: sperm cell
curios.fact: A sperm cell is a specialized motile reproductive cell.

name: Microbe Meadow
quip: One drop can hold a whole neighborhood
lesson: Micrometre-scale life includes bacteria, archaea, protists, and microscopic algae with radically different body plans. A round blob is not a universal microbe shape.

curios.name: E. coli bacterium
curios.fact: Escherichia coli cells are typically rod-shaped bacteria with flexible flagella on many strains.

curios.name: cyanobacterium
curios.fact: Many cyanobacteria form chains or colonies and perform oxygen-producing photosynthesis.

curios.name: diatom
curios.fact: Diatoms build intricate silica cell walls with species-specific geometry.

curios.name: paramecium
curios.fact: Paramecia are single-celled ciliates whose many beating cilia drive movement and feeding.

name: Fiber & Pollen
lesson: Hair widths, pollen grains, tiny multicellular organisms, and large cells overlap around tens to hundreds of micrometres.

curios.name: pollen grain
curios.fact: Pollen sizes and surface textures vary dramatically among plant species.

curios.name: hair fiber
curios.fact: Human hair diameter commonly spans tens of micrometres.

curios.name: paper fiber
curios.fact: Paper is a tangled network of plant-derived cellulose fibers.

curios.name: tardigrade
curios.fact: Many tardigrades are visible under a microscope and are multicellular animals.

curios.name: moss spore
curios.fact: Spores are reproductive cells whose sizes and structures vary widely.

curios.name: skin flake
curios.fact: Many dust particles are fragments of biological material, including shed skin.

curios.name: fungal hypha
curios.fact: Hyphae are branching filaments that form much of a fungus.

curios.name: tiny nematode
curios.fact: Nematodes span a huge size range; the smallest are microscopic multicellular animals.

name: Dust Country
lesson: Household dust is a mixture, not one substance: fibers, soil, skin fragments, pollen, soot, and other particles all contribute.

curios.name: dust mite
curios.fact: Dust mites are animals typically a fraction of a millimetre long.

curios.name: sand grain
curios.fact: Geologists commonly classify sand grains from about 0.0625 to 2 millimetres.

curios.name: fabric lint
curios.fact: Lint is a loose tangle of fibers shed from textiles.

curios.name: crumb
curios.fact: A crumb is already an irregular aggregate of many substances.

curios.name: soot fleck
curios.fact: Soot contains carbon-rich particles produced by incomplete combustion.

curios.name: salt crystal
curios.fact: Table salt crystals form a cubic ionic lattice.

curios.name: insect scale
curios.fact: Butterfly and moth wings are covered with tiny overlapping scales.

curios.name: microplastic
curios.fact: Microplastics are plastic particles smaller than five millimetres.

name: Granule Ground
quip: The specks are big enough to cast opinions
lesson: Millimetre-scale grains bridge dust and hand-held objects. Shape, porosity, and surface texture now dominate how pieces roll and pack together.

curios.name: rice grain
curios.fact: A rice grain is an elongated seed whose size and shape depend on its variety.

curios.name: lentil
curios.fact: A lentil is a flattened lens-shaped seed rather than a miniature sphere.

curios.name: hail pellet
curios.fact: Small hailstones grow as layered ice while moving through storm updrafts.

curios.name: glass bead
curios.fact: Manufactured beads show how regular millimetre-scale geometry differs from natural grains.

name: Pocket World
lesson: At centimetre scales, rigid-body rolling becomes a reasonable visual metaphor—though the magical sticking remains the game's central fiction.

curios.name: pebble
curios.fact: Pebbles are rock fragments rounded or worn by transport and weathering.

curios.name: button
curios.fact: Manufactured objects introduce standardized shapes and materials.

curios.name: toy brick
curios.fact: A familiar rigid object can now visibly protrude from the mash.

curios.name: bottle cap
curios.fact: Thin, asymmetric objects make the rolling body increasingly uneven.

curios.name: coin
curios.fact: Coins are thin metal discs whose familiar size makes a useful centimetre-scale reference.

curios.name: house key
curios.fact: A key's thin teeth create an especially uneven protrusion.

curios.name: six-sided die
curios.fact: A standard gaming die is a small cube with numbered faces.

curios.name: glass marble
curios.fact: A marble is a manufactured glass sphere, often around a centimetre across.

name: Tabletop Trek
quip: The surface is a landscape now
lesson: At decimetre scales, ordinary desk and kitchen objects become recognizable terrain. Hollow and thin objects can have large footprints without comparable gameplay bulk.

curios.name: pencil
curios.fact: A pencil is a long wooden composite built around a graphite-rich writing core.

curios.name: coffee mug
curios.fact: A mug is a hollow ceramic vessel whose handle creates a distinctive side loop.

curios.name: paperback book
curios.fact: A closed paperback is a layered block of paper joined along one flexible spine.

curios.name: tablespoon
curios.fact: A spoon combines a shallow bowl with a long narrow handle.

name: Everyday Kingdom
lesson: The scale now ranges through familiar human-sized objects. The mash becomes visibly irregular and its rolling axis changes as objects accumulate.

curios.name: shoe
curios.fact: Shoes combine flexible fabrics, foams, and rigid structural elements.

curios.name: floor lamp
curios.fact: Long objects can make the rolling mash temporarily elongated.

curios.name: chair
curios.fact: Furniture creates lopsided collisions and prominent silhouettes.

curios.name: couch
curios.fact: Upholstered furniture is mostly empty space, padding, and a structural frame.

curios.name: guitar
curios.fact: An acoustic guitar's hollow body amplifies vibrating strings.

curios.name: kitchen table
curios.fact: A table is mostly empty space bounded by a top and supporting legs.

curios.name: television
curios.fact: A modern flat-panel display is thin relative to its width.

curios.name: potted plant
curios.fact: A potted plant combines living tissue, soil, water, air, and a container.

name: Room Scale
quip: Walls, doors, and the route outside
lesson: A room is a nested container holding furniture, people, air, and all smaller layers already visited. Doorways turn indoor scale into outdoor traversal.

curios.name: bed
curios.fact: A bed is a raised frame supporting flexible layered materials and a mostly hollow space beneath.

curios.name: refrigerator
curios.fact: A refrigerator is an insulated cabinet surrounding pumps, coils, shelves, and air.

curios.name: bathtub
curios.fact: A bathtub is a hollow basin whose familiar footprint is much larger than its material volume.

curios.name: doorway
curios.fact: A doorway is an opening in a wall and a useful transition between nested environments.

name: Vehicle Yard
quip: Traffic has become a food group
lesson: Cars, trucks, boats, and small structures share metre-to-tens-of-metres scales, with mass varying far more than length alone suggests.

curios.name: bicycle
curios.fact: A bicycle is mostly open space, which exposes the difference between size and mass.

curios.name: compact car
curios.fact: A passenger car is several metres long but contains substantial empty interior volume.

curios.name: delivery van
curios.fact: Vehicles make the mash wider and more mechanically awkward.

curios.name: city bus
curios.fact: A bus is long enough to reshape the entire rolling silhouette.

curios.name: motorcycle
curios.fact: A motorcycle is much narrower and lighter than a car of similar length.

curios.name: pickup truck
curios.fact: A pickup combines a passenger cab with an open cargo bed.

curios.name: sailboat
curios.fact: A sailboat converts aerodynamic force on its sails into motion through water.

curios.name: fire engine
curios.fact: Emergency vehicles carry specialized equipment and large water or ladder systems.

name: House & Yard
lesson: Homes sit inside yards, streets, drainage, vegetation, and neighboring structures. The building is no longer the world; it is one object inside a larger place.

curios.name: garden shed
curios.fact: A small shed is a framed enclosure whose walls hide mostly empty interior volume.

curios.name: oak tree
curios.fact: A mature tree is a branching living structure rooted in soil and filled with transport tissue.

curios.name: garage
curios.fact: A garage is a vehicle-sized room connected to a driveway and the surrounding street network.

curios.name: backyard pool
curios.fact: A pool is a lined container whose visible volume is mostly water rather than structure.

name: Built Environment
lesson: Buildings are composite systems with large empty volumes. Length scale is the game's progression measure, not a claim that equal-sized objects have equal mass.

curios.name: bungalow
curios.fact: A house is a structural shell enclosing mostly air.

curios.name: water tower
curios.fact: Infrastructure mixes large dimensions with specialized functions.

curios.name: office block
curios.fact: A building contains many smaller-scale systems the game has already traversed.

curios.name: stadium
curios.fact: At this point the mash is a moving landscape of accumulated structures.

curios.name: townhouse
curios.fact: Attached townhouses share walls while remaining separate dwellings.

curios.name: lighthouse
curios.fact: Lighthouses elevate a navigational light above surrounding terrain and water.

curios.name: suspension bridge
curios.fact: Suspension bridges carry their deck using cables anchored at both ends.

curios.name: skyscraper
curios.fact: Tall buildings must resist wind as well as support their own weight.

name: City Streets
lesson: Cities are connected networks of streets, blocks, utilities, buildings, parks, and people. A skyline alone is not a city; the spaces between structures make it traversable.

curios.name: apartment tower
curios.fact: A residential tower stacks many rooms around shared structure, services, stairs, and elevators.

curios.name: city train
curios.fact: Urban rail vehicles follow connected tracks rather than moving as isolated road traffic.

curios.name: park block
curios.fact: An urban park is a managed open space embedded in the surrounding street grid.

curios.name: river bridge
curios.fact: A city bridge carries a connected route across water, rail, or another road.

name: Landscape Scale
lesson: Mountains, islands, lakes, and cities span kilometres to hundreds of kilometres. Geological objects do not have crisp boundaries.

curios.name: hill
curios.fact: A hill is a landform category without one universal size cutoff.

curios.name: small island
curios.fact: Islands are exposed land surrounded by water; their submerged structure continues below sea level.

curios.name: mountain
curios.fact: Mountain height is tiny compared with Earth's radius.

curios.name: metro area
curios.fact: Urban areas blend continuously into their surroundings.

curios.name: volcano
curios.fact: A volcano is a geological vent and the landform built around it.

curios.name: glacier
curios.fact: Glaciers are flowing bodies of compacted ice.

curios.name: canyon
curios.fact: Canyons are erosional landforms rather than separate solid objects.

curios.name: megacity
curios.fact: A megacity is a dense human system whose boundary depends on the definition used.

name: Regional Map
quip: Roads thin into lines and cities into texture
lesson: At regional scales, rivers, forests, coastlines, weather systems, and urban networks become the readable structure. The city remains present as a small patch inside the land.

curios.name: river basin
curios.fact: A drainage basin is the land area whose water flows toward a shared outlet.

curios.name: forest belt
curios.fact: A forest seen regionally is a mosaic of habitats, disturbances, waterways, and human land use.

curios.name: lake system
curios.fact: Connected lakes and rivers form networks shaped by geology and water flow.

curios.name: storm front
curios.fact: A weather front is a moving boundary between air masses, not a solid object.

name: Moon Scale
quip: Whole worlds fit before Earth does
lesson: Moons and dwarf planets span hundreds to thousands of kilometres. Gravity rounds the largest bodies while smaller ones retain irregular shapes.

curios.name: Ceres
curios.fact: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and is massive enough to be rounded by gravity.

curios.name: Europa
curios.fact: Europa is an icy moon of Jupiter with strong evidence for a subsurface ocean.

curios.name: Earth's Moon
curios.fact: The Moon is about 3,475 kilometres across and tidally locked to Earth.

curios.name: Pluto
curios.fact: Pluto is a dwarf planet with a nitrogen-rich surface and a large moon named Charon.

name: Planetary Pantry
lesson: Earth is about 12,742 km in diameter. Planetary shapes are governed strongly by gravity, becoming nearly spherical above sufficient mass.

curios.name: small moon
curios.fact: Many small moons are irregular because their gravity is too weak to make them round.

curios.name: Mercury
curios.fact: Mercury is the smallest planet in our Solar System.

curios.name: Earth
curios.fact: Earth is an oblate spheroid, slightly wider at the equator.

curios.name: gas giant
curios.fact: Gas giants have no simple solid surface like Earth's.

curios.name: asteroid
curios.fact: Most asteroids are irregular rocky or metallic bodies.

curios.name: comet nucleus
curios.fact: A comet nucleus is a dark mixture of ice, dust, and rock.

curios.name: Mars
curios.fact: Mars is a rocky planet with a diameter a little over half Earth's.

curios.name: Saturn
curios.fact: Saturn is a gas giant surrounded by a broad, thin ring system.

name: Giant Worlds
lesson: Giant planets are dominated by deep atmospheres and fluid interiors. Rings and moons make each planet the center of a nested local system.

curios.name: Jupiter
curios.fact: Jupiter is the Solar System's largest planet and has a deep atmosphere dominated by hydrogen and helium.

curios.name: Saturn
curios.fact: Saturn's broad rings are made from countless orbiting particles rather than a solid disc.

curios.name: Uranus
curios.fact: Uranus rotates on its side relative to its orbit and has a cold hydrogen-helium-methane atmosphere.

curios.name: Neptune
curios.fact: Neptune is an ice giant with powerful winds and a deep blue atmospheric appearance.

name: Stellar Buffet
lesson: Stars are self-gravitating plasma spheres powered for most of their lives by nuclear fusion. Their sizes vary enormously.

curios.name: red dwarf
curios.fact: Red dwarfs are cool, low-mass stars and the most common stellar type.

curios.name: Sun-like star
curios.fact: The Sun is about 1.39 million km in diameter.

curios.name: blue giant
curios.fact: Hot, massive stars burn fuel quickly and live comparatively short lives.

curios.name: red supergiant
curios.fact: Some supergiants would extend beyond Earth's orbit if placed at the Sun.

curios.name: white dwarf
curios.fact: A white dwarf is the dense remnant core left by many low- and medium-mass stars.

curios.name: neutron star
curios.fact: Neutron stars pack more mass than the Sun into a city-sized sphere.

curios.name: orange subgiant
curios.fact: A subgiant has exhausted hydrogen in its core and begun expanding.

curios.name: blue hypergiant
curios.fact: Hypergiants are extremely luminous, massive, and short-lived stars.

name: System Sweep
lesson: A planetary system is mostly empty space. Visual sizes and distances must be compressed differently or the planets would be nearly invisible.

curios.name: planetary system
curios.fact: Orbital systems are bound by gravity, not enclosed by a physical shell.

curios.name: binary stars
curios.fact: Many stars are members of binary or multiple systems.

curios.name: Oort-cloud analogue
curios.fact: The distant Oort Cloud is inferred from comet orbits, not directly imaged as a shell.

curios.name: rogue planet
curios.fact: Some planets travel through interstellar space without orbiting a star.

curios.name: asteroid belt
curios.fact: An asteroid belt is a broad population of separate orbiting objects, not a dense ring.

curios.name: protoplanetary disk
curios.fact: Planets form within rotating disks of gas and dust around young stars.

curios.name: triple-star system
curios.fact: Stable hierarchical systems can contain three or more gravitationally bound stars.

curios.name: Kuiper-belt analogue
curios.fact: Icy small bodies can occupy broad regions beyond a system's major planets.

name: Stellar Neighborhood
quip: Stars become points inside a shared cloud
lesson: Light-years separate neighboring stars. Clusters, nebulae, and molecular clouds reveal structure between a planetary system and an entire galaxy.

curios.name: open star cluster
curios.fact: Open clusters are loose groups of stars formed from the same molecular cloud.

curios.name: globular cluster
curios.fact: Globular clusters are dense, roughly spherical populations of old stars.

curios.name: emission nebula
curios.fact: An emission nebula glows when energetic starlight ionizes surrounding gas.

curios.name: molecular cloud
curios.fact: Cold molecular clouds are dense interstellar regions where new stars can form.

name: Galaxy Garden
lesson: Galaxies contain stars, gas, dust, compact objects, and dark matter. Their visible edges are not hard boundaries.

curios.name: dwarf galaxy
curios.fact: Dwarf galaxies can contain millions to billions of stars.

curios.name: spiral galaxy
curios.fact: Spiral arms are density patterns, not permanent rows of the same stars.

curios.name: elliptical galaxy
curios.fact: Elliptical galaxies range from dwarfs to giants.

curios.name: galaxy cluster
curios.fact: Galaxy clusters are the largest gravitationally bound structures.

curios.name: irregular galaxy
curios.fact: Irregular galaxies lack a dominant spiral or elliptical structure.

curios.name: barred spiral
curios.fact: Many spiral galaxies have a central bar-shaped stellar structure.

curios.name: active galaxy
curios.fact: An active galactic nucleus is powered by matter falling toward a supermassive black hole.

curios.name: galaxy group
curios.fact: Galaxy groups are smaller gravitationally bound collections than rich clusters.

name: Galaxy Cluster Web
quip: Galaxies become beads on enormous filaments
lesson: Galaxy groups and clusters trace a large-scale web shaped by gravity and dark matter. Voids and filaments are regions of a continuous cosmic distribution, not hard-edged objects.

curios.name: Local Group
curios.fact: The Local Group contains the Milky Way, Andromeda, Triangulum, and many smaller galaxies.

curios.name: Virgo Cluster
curios.fact: The Virgo Cluster is the nearest large galaxy cluster and contains well over a thousand member galaxies.

curios.name: cosmic void
curios.fact: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions surrounded by denser filaments and walls.

curios.name: supercluster strand
curios.fact: Supercluster-scale associations trace the cosmic web but are not generally bound as one object.

name: Observable Universe
quip: The edge is a horizon, not a wall
lesson: The observable universe is limited by how far light has reached us, not by a known physical boundary of the whole universe.

curios.name: cosmic web region
curios.fact: Matter forms a web of filaments and voids on the largest mapped scales.

curios.name: observable horizon
curios.fact: Different observers have different observable universes.

curios.name: great void
curios.fact: Cosmic voids are underdense, not perfectly empty.

curios.name: causal patch
curios.fact: Causality limits which regions can influence one another.

curios.name: cosmic filament
curios.fact: Galaxies and dark matter trace enormous filaments around cosmic voids.

curios.name: supercluster region
curios.fact: Superclusters describe large associations that are not generally bound as single objects.

curios.name: last-scattering patch
curios.fact: The cosmic microwave background comes from the era when the universe became transparent.

curios.name: Hubble volume
curios.fact: A Hubble volume is a cosmological scale related to the universe's expansion rate.

name: Metaversal Beyond
lesson: There is no established scientific 'metaversal' length scale. Everything beyond the observable-universe milestone is explicitly imaginative and infinite.

curios.name: pocket reality
curios.fact: A pocket reality is speculative fiction, not an observed object.

curios.name: alternate history
